goal: Iske baad aap 1..n ka sum, power, Fibonacci, gcd aur kisi number ke digits ke liye recursive functions likh aur trace kar sakte hain, bata sakte hain ke kisi problem ke liye kaunsa version (loop ya recursion) theek hai, aur samjha sakte hain ke Fibonacci mein kaam baar baar kyun repeat hota hai.
warmup: Ek cousin aap ko Rs 500 ka note deta hai aur kehta hai: "Mujhe is tarah wapas karna: kal se aap ki Eid salami aur uske baad jo bhi aap ka udhaar bache." Total jaanne ke liye aap ko sirf aaj ki raqam aur baqi ka total chahiye. Aap ek tukra alag karte hain aur chhoti problem aage de dete hain, jab tak kuch bacha na rahe. Numbers ki bohat si problems, jaise 1 se n tak add karna ya ek ek digit kaatna, bilkul aisi hi hoti hain.
definition: Recursive solution hamesha ek hi recipe follow karta hai. Step 1: sab se chhoti problem dhoondein jis ka jawab foran mil jaye (base case). Step 2: batayein ke bari problem ek zara chhoti problem se kaise banti hai (recursive case). Step 3: check karein ke har call chhoti hoti jaye, taake woh lazmi base case tak pohanch jaye. Yeh lesson is recipe ko chhe classic problems par lagata hai.
howItWorks: 1) 1..n ka sum: sumTo(n) = n + sumTo(n - 1), base sumTo(0) = 0. 2) Power: power(base, exp) = base * power(base, exp - 1), base power(base, 0) = 1. 3) Number ko ulta print karna: aakhri digit n % 10 print karein, phir n / 10 (yani aakhri digit ke baghair number) par recurse karein; base n == 0. Agar aap digit ko recursive call ke BAAD print karein to normal order mil jata hai. 4) Digits ka sum: n % 10 + sumDigits(n / 10). 5) Euclid ka gcd: a aur b ka greatest common divisor, b aur a % b ke gcd ke barabar hota hai; jab b 0 ho to jawab a hai. Yeh wohi idea hai jo Euclid ke purane tareeqe mein tha: divide karo aur remainder rakho. 6) Fibonacci: sequence 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 ... jis mein har number pichle do numbers ka sum hota hai: fib(n) = fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2), bases fib(0) = 0 aur fib(1) = 1. FIBONACCI MEIN KAAM BAAR BAAR KYUN HOTA HAI: har call do aur calls banati hai, is liye wohi chhoti values baar baar calculate hoti hain. fib(5) ke visual mein fib(3) do dafa aur fib(2) teen dafa nikala jata hai. Hamare counter ne dikhaya ke fib(6) ko 25 calls chahiye, halanke sirf 7 alag values chahiye. Bare n ke liye yeh bohat slow ho jata hai (fib(40) 30 crore se zyada calls karta hai), is liye Fibonacci ke liye loop kahin behtar hai. PALINDROME KA IDEA (aisa lafz jo ulta bhi waisa hi parha jaye, jaise level): pehla aur aakhri character compare karein. Agar different hon to jawab no hai. Agar match karein to beech ke chhote lafz ko check karein. Length 0 ya 1 wala lafz hamesha palindrome hota hai (base case). Strings ke lessons mein hum iske liye simple loop use karte hain, lekin recursive idea wohi peel-off pattern hai. TAIL-STYLE SOCH: gcd mein recursive call function ka bilkul AAKHRI kaam hai, aur baad mein kuch add ya multiply karna baqi nahi hota. Jab jawab wapas aata hai to stack par koi zaroori cheez nahi bachi hoti, is liye aise function ko loop mein likhna aasaan hai (while (b != 0) { ... }). Factorial aur sumTo different hain: call wapas aane ke baad unhein abhi multiply ya add karna hota hai, is liye har frame ko intezar karna parta hai. Rule yeh hai: simple repeat ke liye loop use karein, aur recursion tab use karein jab problem khud apni chhoti copies se define hoti ho.
